'''Thawa'''{{refn|group=note|name=first|Sometimes spelt ''Thaua'', ''Dhawa'', ''Thauaira'', and other variations.}} is a nearly extinct [[Australian Aboriginal language]] of [[New South Wales]] with only very few speakers including certain local [[Aboriginal elder|elders]]. It is sometimes classified with [[Dyirringany language|Dyirringany]] as a dialect of [[Southern Coastal Yuin]], though it is not clear how close the two varieties actually were.<ref name="AIATSIS" />

In 2015 local Yuin people collaborated with the Tathra Public School in [[Tathra, New South Wales|Tathra]] to create a new [[mobile app|app]] as a teaching aid for both Thawa and the [[Dhurga language]], using old [[audio recording]]s of [[Aboriginal elder|elders]] as well as documentation created by early explorers and settlers in the region. One of the major contributors to the project, Graham Moore, has also written an Aboriginal language book.<ref>{{cite web | last=Brown | first=Bill | title=Yuin elders develop 'message stick' app to teach almost-lost Aboriginal language  | website=ABC News| publisher= [[Australian Broadcasting Corporation]] | date=16 October 2015 | url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2015-10-16/aboriginal-language-app-preserves-language/6834724 | access-date=21 June 2021}}</ref>
